Looking at Arc resolution, what it actually does is that it translates `T` into plain `Object` and does resolution on top of that. E.g. in time of comparison, it compares required type `ConcurrentGaugedMethodBean<Long>)` with bean that has `ConcurrentGaugedMethodBean<Object>)` and according to [CDI spec](https://docs.jboss.org/cdi/spec/2.0/cdi-spec.html#assignable_parameters) this then falls under:

> the required type parameter and the bean type parameter are actual types with identical raw type, and, if the type is parameterized, the bean type parameter is assignable to the required type parameter according to these rules, or

issue.title: Arquillian adapter - @Before and @After callbacks are not invoked
issue.body:
It seems that Arquillian's `ClientBeforeAfterLifecycleEventExecuter` invokes the callbacks only if `org.jboss.arquillian.container.test.impl.client.protocol.local.LocalProtocol` is used. Which is not the case for Quarkus.

See
https://github.com/arquillian/arquillian-core/blob/master/container/test-impl-base/src/main/java/org/jboss/arquillian/container/test/impl/execution/ClientBeforeAfterLifecycleEventExecuter.java#L65
and
https://github.com/arquillian/arquillian-core/blob/master/container/test-impl-base/src/main/java/org/jboss/arquillian/container/test/impl/RunModeUtils.java#L112

In theory, we should be able to invoke the callbacks ourselves. 

There is one problem though. The callbacks are invoked on the original test class whereas the test methods are invoked upon a "enhanced" test class loaded by the app class loader (`RuntimeClassLoader`). In other words, we could invoke the callbacks but it would be useless (e.g. it would not be possible to assert the static members set in the callbacks).
